You are a skeptical fact-checker for a restaurant directory (eatdanville.com). Three restaurants in downtown Danville, California were researched: Rancho Cantina (501 Hartz Ave), Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar (480 Hartz Ave) and Danville Harvest. The researcher output is in the JSON file C:/Users/Kenneth Rodas/Documents/GitHub/eatdanville/data/research/round1.journal.json: read it with the Read tool (each entry's result has official_name, address, phone, hours, services, signature_dishes, signature_drinks, links).
Tools: use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). You may also use Bash with curl (e.g. curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" URL | head -c 200000) to read pages that WebFetch cannot, and curl -sI to check headers. Do NOT use any browser tools (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__claude-in-chrome__*); the browser tab is reserved. Never guess: every fact must come from a page you actually read. If something cannot be found, leave it empty and say so in notes. Do not invent hours, prices, or dishes.
For EACH of the three restaurants, verify independently against at least two sources the researcher did not rely on where possible (Google Business listing via search snippets, Yelp, OpenTable/Resy/Toast pages, Facebook page info, the town business directory, recent press):
(a) LISTING DATA: official name, address, phone, weekly hours, latest close time, price range, reservation/ordering links and social handles. Hours matter most: this site promotes 8-10pm business, so confirm each night's closing time and whether the bar stays open later than the kitchen.
(b) MENU AND SERVICE CLAIMS: every service boolean (brunch, lunch, dinner, late night, private dining, catering, takeout, delivery, happy hour, secret menu, industry specials, patio, live music, kids menu) by reading the actual menu/event/catering pages, and that the listed signature dishes, drinks and desserts appear on the current menu with those prices. Flag anything stale, invented or copied from a different location of the same brand. Add notable items the researcher missed (dessert menu, nightcap cocktails, digestivi, tasting menus, wine nights, brunch hours, private room capacity).
Report corrections with a source URL for each, confirmed fields, unverifiable fields and additions, per restaurant (key = rancho-cantina, kaias, harvest). Default to flagging rather than accepting when evidence is thin. Return only the structured object.

Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.

- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-claude: Guided setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

29:What sets this spot apart is not only the inviting atmosphere but also the standout dishes that define its menu. The Fried Chicken Sandwich, for example, is a crowd favorite—crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and perfectly seasoned. Pair it with a cup of their rich, aromatic coffee, and you’ve got a combo that hits all the right notes whether it’s for breakfast or a casual lunch.
31:The menu at Danville Harvest shines because of its balance between indulgence and health-conscious options. This makes it a perfect choice whether you’re stopping by for a romantic dinner or a casual meal out. Plus, the outdoor seating area adds to the relaxed vibe, where you can enjoy your food while soaking up the California sun.
33:Visitors often highlight not only the fantastic food but also the charming and friendly service. Reviews mention that the staff takes the time to make guests feel at home, adding a personal touch to every visit. Whether you’re trying the short ribs in the evening or stopping by for a morning coffee and sandwich, Danville Harvest feels like a local gem worth discovering.

136:We wandered in for a late lunch and were so glad we did. Their happy hour is excellent — great deals on both drinks and small bites. The patio is spacious and shaded with big umbrellas and string lights, while the inside is just as charming with warm, stylish details. The whole place smelled amazing when we walked in. The menu is fresh and California-inspired, with plenty of healthy options alongside heartier dishes. We loved the variety — from shrimp lettuce wraps and crab cakes to salads, sliders, and seasonal plates. Cocktails are creative and well-balanced, and the wine list has a thoughtful mix of local and international picks. Danville Harvest is the perfect spot whether you’re looking for a relaxed happy hour or a full meal. We’ll definitely be back.
138:Found Danville Harvest off of Yelp. Two of us ordered: field work pulp hazy IPA $8 ea bloodrot pinot $14 ea brussels sprouts $15 short rib entree $29 steak frites $31 Entrees a bit on pricier side, but ingredients were good. Parking can be tough during peak hours, but there is a lot in the back.
139:Arthur T
140:I’m not from the area and drove past this cute corner restaurant and decide to give it a try. It was a Wednesday around 12:40pm. Parking was a bit challenging but that could be because I’m unfamiliar with the area. At first glance the restaurant appears “average” but once you walk in and see/feel the atmosphere, that perception instantly changes. It was a lot more “upscale” than I had expected (especially since I had a baby with me which automatically made me feel uncomfortable.) When I was greeted, the first thing I was asked was if I had a reservation (which totally caught me off guard). I did not have one, however the friendly employee by the name of Daniel, sat me and my baby outside on the patio which ended up working out great for us. Since I had my 1 1/2 year old with me in his stroller it really was the best option, plus it was a gorgeous afternoon! Daniel also ended up being my waiter and instantly made me feel welcome there. He even assisted me with my son’s stroller as to help us get to our patio table (which by the way was an adorable, comfy sofa styled set). On to the food: I chose the ravioli and let me say, it was DELICIOUS! I highly recommend. For my little guy, there wasn’t too much for his age category (totally understandable) so he had the chicken strips (which were home made style) and he did love them. Price: yes, this restaurant is definitely on the pricey side, but again, I am not from the area and so this may just be what is normal for Danville, Ca. All and all, I would say, it’s not very kids/family friendly however, I’d love to return one day to have a date there with my husband. Thank you again Daniel for doing your best to make mine and my baby’s experience there as pleasant and enjoyable as possible, you truly were a pleasure.
142:Had an amazing brunch at Danville Harvest with my fiancée, and it definitely lived up to the hype. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, with a charming rustic farmhouse vibe that makes you feel right at home. We started with coffee and fresh-squeezed juice, both excellent. For food, I had the braised short rib hash, which was packed with flavor—perfectly tender meat, crispy potatoes, and a runny egg to tie it all together. My fiancée went with the lemon ricotta pancakes, and they were next-level—fluffy, slightly tangy, and topped with just the right amount of syrup and fresh berries. Service was spot on—friendly, attentive, and never rushed. You can tell they focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients, and it makes all the difference. Definitely a spot we’ll be coming back to, whether for a relaxed brunch date or a weekend treat. Highly recommend!

Danville Harvest offers upscale style and ambiance in a premier downtown venue. Whether you’re planning a corporate party, rehearsal dinner, or baby shower, the ideal setting for your private event can be found in one of our four private event spaces.

and share key details - preferred date(s), time, guest count, occasion, etc. Our Events Manager will ensure your event is a success!
Front Bar Dining
Located in the front of the restaurant adjacent to the bar area, the Front Bar is a fun and lively setting perfect for happy hours and casual gatherings amongst family and friends. This space is ideal for a casual reception of up to 24 guests.
Main Dining Room
Our main dining room is ideal for larger gatherings and more formal dinners - up to 48 seated guests or up to 70 guests for a standing reception. The back section can also be curtained off for a private dining experience for up to 20 guests.
Side Patio
This area is a cozy al fresco patio that can accommodate up to 26 seated guests or 36 guests for a standing reception.
Full Restaurant

restaurants.notes: Sources used that the researcher did not: danville-harvest.res-discover.com read directly for the full Google Business attribute set and day-by-day hours (they cited the URL but never pulled the services/highlights payload), visittrivalley.com, lovetrivalley.com, and a fresh pdftotext extraction of all four June 2026 menu PDFs plus a fresh read of /contact and /events. The menu and happy-hour transcription in the journal is accurate — I found no invented dish, no wrong price, and no item copied from a sibling restaurant. The defects are all on the listing side: the claim that the official site publishes no open/close times is simply false; the day-by-day hours are presented as settled when four sources disagree by up to 90 minutes on exactly the nights this directory cares about; the owner attribution has no first-party support; and three dessert prices are DoorDash markups presented as menu facts. restaurants.additions:
THE CONTACT-PAGE HOURS BLOCK is itself the most important addition — "Weekdays 11:30am–9pm / Weekends 10am–10pm" is a second, later, first-party hours statement the journal never captured, and it is the only official source supporting a 10pm weekend close.

ZERO-PROOF COCKTAILS, a whole missing category at $13: Blueberry Crush (blueberry, lime, rosemary, ginger ale, pea-flower water), Blackberry Bramble (N/A gin, blackberry, orgeat, lime, basil), Mint Condition (N/A gin, apple, cinnamon, orange, mint, ginger beer). N/A beer too: Fieldwork Grapefruit Blonde or IPA 7, Erdinger 5.

COCKTAILS OMITTED: Solstice (vodka, earl grey, lemon, mint), Farmer's Punch (rum, strawberry-kiwi, orgeat, lime, angostura, mint), Just Beachy (vodka, pineapple, lime, honey, toasted coconut, ginger beer), Golden Orchard (white whiskey, golden raisin, apricot, marigold liqueur, almond), Violet Hour (gin, aloe, plum, sichuan peppercorn, butterfly pea flower).

WINE IS POURED IN TWO SIZES — 6oz and 9oz, priced as a pair (Argiolas Vermentino 14/22, BloodRoot Chardonnay 15/23, Rivers-Marie Chardonnay 19/27, Three Sticks Pinot Noir 19/27, Teeter-Totter Cabernet 20/28, Brut Blanc de Blancs 16/24). That format is a genuine listing differentiator and is nowhere in the journal.

DINNER ITEMS MISSED: starters Gazpacho 12, Deviled Eggs 13, Roasted Cauliflower 13, Italian Meatballs 15, Shrimp & Succotash 18, Avocado Bruschetta 15, Ahi Tuna Poke 21, Burrata Toast 14, Shrimp Lettuce Cups 16; salads Heirloom Tomato 19, Superfood 18, Chopped 17, Farmhouse Caesar 21; mains Grain Bowl 22, Roasted Chicken 29, Gnocchi Ragu 24, Summer Ravioli 26, Grilled Pork Chop 32; add-ons Grilled Shrimp 11, Steak 15, Salmon 14, Grilled Chicken 8, Crispy Parmesan Chicken 9, truffle fries 12, sweet potato fries 10.

HAPPY-HOUR-ONLY ITEMS MISSED: Smashburger 16 (two patties, secret sauce, fries; +bacon 4) appears only on the happy-hour menu, plus Tempura Green Beans 13, Deviled Eggs 13, and happy-hour-priced Chopped Salad 16 and Superfood Salad 17.

BRUNCH ITEMS MISSED: Cheddar Biscuits 12, Fruit Bowl 12, Avocado Toast 16, Country Breakfast Plate 17, Breakfast Skillet 19, Fried Chicken & Waffles 23, Ham Benedict 18, Golden Sourdough Stack 19, Chorizo Tostada 19, Breakfast Sandwich 17, Huevos Rancheros 19, Chicken Salad Sandwich 15, Smoked Turkey Sandwich 16.

BEER: six drafts all $8 (Mother Earth Cali Creamin cream ale, Coronado Salty Crew blonde, East Brothers Bo Pils, Humble Sea helles, Fieldwork hazy IPA, Laughing Monk rotating WC IPA), cans $6–8, Sincere Bonafide dry cider 6.

GOOGLE ATTRIBUTES worth surfacing: fireplace, LGBTQ+ friendly, family friendly, good for groups, cosy/romantic/upmarket, "brunch, lunch and dinner reservations recommended," and a free parking lot behind the restaurant (repeatedly cited in reviews as the fix for tight street parking).

DATA-QUALITY WARNING for future ingest: lovetrivalley.com/places/danville-harvest publishes a WRONG phone number, (925) 743-4278, and shows Thursday and Friday as "Closed." It is an unclaimed listing. Do not ingest it.
restaurants.notes: Sources used that the researcher did not: danville-harvest.res-discover.com read directly for the full Google Business attribute set and day-by-day hours (they cited the URL but never pulled the services/highlights payload), visittrivalley.com, lovetrivalley.com, and a fresh pdftotext extraction of all four June 2026 menu PDFs plus a fresh read of /contact and /events. The menu and happy-hour transcription in the journal is accurate — I found no invented dish, no wrong price, and no item copied from a sibling restaurant. The defects are all on the listing side: the claim that the official site publishes no open/close times is simply false; the day-by-day hours are presented as settled when four sources disagree by up to 90 minutes on exactly the nights this directory cares about; the owner attribution has no first-party support; and three dessert prices are DoorDash markups presented as menu facts. Yelp, OpenTable, Tripadvisor, Uber Eats, order.online, wheree and BringFido all returned 403/CAPTCHA to every method, so the rating figures in the journal remain snippet-sourced and should carry that caveat on the live site.
